mostWorthwhile.text: Making tides connected the moon to the ocean in an evocative way, while clearly acknowledging both lunar and solar gravity.

leastWorthwhile.text: Applying gravity twice to reach the moon felt routine, especially when the first application produced another intermediate.

surprise.text: Rain and crust producing basins surprised me, though their subsequent role in holding water was clear.

arbitrary.text: Rain producing basins felt somewhat unexplained: the result gave little sense of how the basins formed, even allowing for mythic compression.

continue.text: Yes. The progression from impact to moon to tidal shore connected events at different scales, and I would be curious to see what the world makes next.
